key_insight: Real-world dexterous evaluation requires integrating perception, context-aware decision-making, and precise hand control rather than testing isolated primitives. DexHoldem provides a system-level benchmark with 1,470 teleoperated demonstrations on a ShadowHand to enable such integrated evaluation.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between isolated dexterous skills and end-to-end embodied manipulation evaluation by offering a real-hardware benchmark that tests perception-to-action pipelines, sequential decision-making, and scene maintenance in a complex tabletop task.
method: Formulate Texas Hold'em card manipulation as a structured testbed composed of 14 manipulation primitives and multi-step rounds.
Collect 1,470 teleoperated demonstrations on a ShadowHand, capturing multimodal perception data and control traces for each primitive and sequence.
Provide task definitions, evaluation protocols, and success metrics focused on sequence completion, scene usability, and robustness on real hardware.
impact: Enables researchers to develop, compare, and benchmark embodied dexterous policies on real hardware, accelerating progress in robust robotic manipulation, policy generalization, and sim-to-real transfer. Offers a standardized dataset and evaluation suite for system-level research.
visual_elements: System pipeline diagram: camera → perception → policy → ShadowHand → updated scene (with icons for each module).
Photo sequence or gif of the ShadowHand executing representative card primitives (deal, push, flip).
Dataset infographic: counts and breakdown (1,470 demos, 14 primitives, demo distribution by primitive).
Timeline/flow diagram of a Texas Hold'em round showing primitive sequence, decision points, and success/failure metrics.
paper_title: DexHoldem: Playing Texas Hold'em with Dexterous Embodied System
paper_authors: Feng Chen, Tianzhe Chu, Li Sun, Pei Zhou, Zhuxiu Xu
